pull_request.body:
## Global envelope baseline — E1-R2, ready for further human review

Review round 2's remaining request was a justified space allowance for a **3 T central solenoid**. E1-R2 reserves **r=1.24–1.64 m, |z|≤3.55 m** and moves adjacent calorimeters outward/downstream. The explicit budget includes 150 mm cold assembly, 200 mm cryostat/interface space and 50 mm integration margin, with 250 mm end allowances. This is a conservative planning allocation, not engineering certification.

[Main proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md) · [Solenoid space budget](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-solenoid-space-budget.md) · [Review 2 disposition](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md) · [Review 1](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-1.md) · [Study catalogue](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/validation/DES-003-study-catalogue.md)

### Working baseline

- 14 TeV HL-LHC; tracker |η|<4, calorimeter |η|<5, muons |η|<3 with 3.5 stretch.
- Detached forward calorimeter included; technology selection follows later.
- Retain **25 mm aggressive tracker host radius**, distinct from active sensor radius.
- Investigate the **outermost tracker layer as the potential timing layer**.
- Detailed magnetic-system and muon setup research come next. ACTS installation is planned for straight-line and full-field propagation.

### Proposed envelope allocations

Metres; reflect positive z to negative z. Maximum radii enclose any future polygon corners. The forward instrumented reservation excludes still-unassigned external support/readout/shielding volumes.

| Allocation | r min–max | absolute z min–max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tracker assembly | 0.025–1.14 | 0–3.15 |
| Tracker interface reserve | 1.14–1.24 | 0–3.15 |
| Coil / cryostat reserve | 1.24–1.64 | 0–3.55 |
| ECal barrel | 1.7–2.06 | 0–3.5 |
| ECal endcaps | 0.18–2.06 | 3.65–4.01 |
| HCal barrel | 2.16–4.2 | 0–4.01 |
| HCal endcaps | 0.2–4.2 | 4.16–6.2 |
| Muon barrel allocation | 4.35–6.762 | 0–7.2 |
| Muon endcap allocation | 0.4–7 | 7.2–10.27 |
| Forward calorimeter reserve | 0.12–1.5 | 11.2–13.2 |

![E1-R2 r–z drawing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/figures/DES-003-envelope-rz.png)

The central radial/axial shifts retain nominal calorimeter thicknesses and shared gaps, reducing the muon barrel host by another 0.20 m. Conditional 16-sided face-normal depths decrease slightly; the main proposal reports that consequence. Detailed magnet design may later amend the reservation; no uniform 3 T field map is claimed.

### Checks and decision scope

- 11 analytic envelope tests and 15 logging/documentation tests passed; 24 session records validated.
- Regenerated drawing/report: 10 allocations, 21 sampled rays, no positive-area rectangle overlaps. Input/script hashes verified and figure inspected.
- No detector transport, field solution, ACTS installation or performance acceptance claimed.

DES-003 and ADR-006 remain **DRAFT**. The requested human decision is the global envelope baseline and its explicit allowances. Subsequent subsystem/field/material work and resulting envelope amendments retain the normal design workflow. Only an identified human may sign off an exact revision. Production geometry and the TDR submodule are unchanged.

E1-R1 adds a detached forward-calorimeter study volume at |z|=11.2–13.2 m, r=0.12–1.50 m. The later consolidated review target of |eta|<5 supersedes the earlier minimum of 4. ATLAS forward calorimetry covers 3.1–4.9; CMS operational literature reports HF to 5.19. The proposed volume has full axial traversal for prompt rays through eta 5, but edge response, beam aperture, shielding and total installed enclosure remain to be established.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md

Added operational ATLAS electron/photon and CMS hadron-calorimeter calibration papers alongside the TDR precedents. CAL-V01/02 now require material scenarios and species/energy/angle leakage studies. Historical depth bands remain screening ranges, not automatic containment requirements; 14 TeV collisions do not imply 14 TeV single-particle tests.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md

Recorded the later consolidated target |eta|<5, which includes this requested minimum. A dedicated forward candidate is now drawn and tested geometrically; extension to 5.2 remains exploratory because its prompt entrance margin is only 3.57 mm.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md

Kept coil ordering and return topology coupled to the muon-system study. E1-R1 still draws an inner-solenoid hypothesis; outer-solenoid, instrumented-return and air-core-toroid alternatives remain. This iteration does not force a dedicated muon magnet decision.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Moved detailed PCB/effective-material inventory behind envelope definition. It still must be included whenever inherited material depth is quoted; deferral is not permission to delete or double-count its mass.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md

Added ATLAS barrel/endcap-gap services (2008 detector paper §5.5, PDF166), CMS ECal end patch panels (§4.2, PDF119), and HGCAL outer-surface/rear-annular exits shared with timing/muons (TDR §4.5, PDF64–65). Proposed route topology: barrel bundles toward end patch regions, endcap bundles toward outer/rear handoffs, with named owners and phi sectors. Capacities and minimal path depth remain ENV-V03/CAL-V02 work.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md

The proposal now calls for minimal but sufficient supports with explicit footprints and material ownership. Forward support, readout and shielding may extend beyond the instrumented box; its bounds are not advertised as a complete installed enclosure.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md

Made polygon shape an optional later component choice. Circular maximum-enclosure bounds remain the planning convention. The 16-sided depth calculation is explicitly conditional, retained only to compare with ODD.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md

Replaced the identification-first preference with a standalone-compatible, potentially toroidal baseline investigation. All three architectures remain in the comparison. Reserving the muon host is not proof that toroid coils, supports and stations fit; dedicated magnet design remains deferred.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Standalone-compatible muon measurement is now the baseline investigation rather than a mandatory finalized requirement. The catalogue separates tracker-combined, vertex-constrained muon-only and unconstrained standalone results, so an outer-coil combined fit cannot silently stand in for independent momentum measurement.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Recorded 14 TeV HL-LHC as the study scenario. CAL-V03/MU-V05 require leakage and punch-through evidence before recommending extra absorber steel. None is added. The detached forward calorimeter is downstream of current muon stations, so smaller upstream endcap apertures are proposed to study filtering at eta 3–3.5; their adequate depth remains unproven.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Recorded tracker |eta|<4, calorimeter |eta|<5 with extension conditional, and muons |eta|<3 with 3.5 stretch. E1-R1 proposes ECal/HCal inner endcap radii 0.18/0.20 m, muon parent 0.40 m and detached forward calorimetry. These are new draft allocations, not achieved acceptance; actual station edges need a later layout.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Added docs/validation/DES-003-study-catalogue.md, including MU-V01–08: stations, independent measurements, vector-field bending, material/transport, punch-through, sensitive hits, reconstruction and systematic variations. Every item lists owners, dependencies, outputs and execution state.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Added later operational calibration evidence. It supports the built scale and coverage but does not certify nODD containment: response corrections, material and leakage still matter. The cross-check also found a real documentation discrepancy: the 2008 CMS paper gives HF outer steel/sensitive radius 1.30 m, while the 2020 calibration paper §2 gives calorimeter radius 1.57 m. Its cause is unresolved and is not silently treated as an upgrade; nODD 1.50 m is an independent design proposal.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md

Built NbTi examples support studying 2–4 T, but not claiming that 3 T fits a complete 200 mm coil/cryostat. For a finite current sheet R=1.34 m, L=6.70 m, 3 T centrally needs about 17.23 MA-turn; magnetic-pressure scale is 3.58 MPa and a uniform-bore energy proxy is 115.9 MJ. The same toy model gives only 1.82 T on axis at z=3.15 m. Winding, reinforcement, thermal/quench systems and return flux need a physical decomposition; these calculations are not a magnet feasibility certificate.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md

Added mandatory PROP-V01 after a field and material/active-surface model exist. It requires full charged-particle propagation, sensitive crossings, numerical convergence and the same field identity in transport and reconstruction. Straight rays remain only the present allocation screen.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/validation/DES-003-study-catalogue.md

Retained E1 central dimensions as the negotiation baseline. E1-R1 changes endcap apertures and adds forward calorimetry in response to the coverage review. The initial proposal is preserved at commit 7bb7ff0; new dimensions remain draft choices.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md

A separate outer barrel timing assembly plus forward disks is the strongest comparison, rather than assuming an ordinary outer strip layer gives precision timing. CMS MTD provides a 40 mm barrel precedent using LYSO/SiPM; ATLAS HGTD provides forward LGAD coverage 2.4–4 with a 125 mm vessel/moderator allocation. Full nODD timing to eta 4 would be a new combined ambition. Coverage needs active-area/vertex/curved-track association, ageing, inefficiency and timing-response studies (TIME-V01); shared service space is not yet partitioned.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md

Retained the overall ODD-like starting scale and documented E1-R1 as a review-driven iteration. This agreement to start is recorded as direction for the investigation, not technical sign-off of numerical dimensions.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md

Dedicated muon-magnet selection/design remains with the later muon-system work. The current plan preserves standalone-compatible space and interface questions while comparing toroidal, solenoidal/combined and instrumented-return options.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

There is no justified universal minimum from collision energy alone. CMS Phase-2 TDR starts active pixels near 29 mm; operating ATLAS IBL provides a 33 mm precedent. We propose screening active radii around 30–35 mm later. The existing 25 mm host boundary is not a sensor radius: the inherited 24.4 mm pipe leaves only 0.6 mm before support, motion and installation allowance. Beam optics/aperture, pipe stability, lifetime/rate and module/support assumptions must set the limit.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md

An outer solenoid can provide useful bending between tracker and muon segments, potentially replacing a separate magnet for a combined measurement. It does not automatically give tracker-independent momentum, particularly for displaced muons. Iron is not fundamentally required: flux can return through air or return coils, but the field/stray-field, energy and support problem changes. Compare signed bending integrals between measured surfaces, field maps, alignment and scattering; CMS operational yoke studies are now catalogued as evidence.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Replaced the open coverage question with the explicit 4/5/3 targets and 3.5 muon stretch. The follow-up now asks whether proposed apertures, transition depth, finite vertices and upstream filtering can deliver those objectives.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md

Expanded the interface register with forward beam/support/shielding and timing ownership. Added literature-based service handoffs and a staged study catalogue. Unassigned space is now clearly a competing allocation to close, especially the timing/service band and forward support beyond the drawn instrumented box.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md

Kept layer/module/station design after envelope definition. The current pass sets coverage/aperture contracts and a first-radius comparison range only; it does not select or implement a tracker layout.

Detached forward calorimetry is now part of the working envelope baseline. Absorber and readout technology selection stays in later calorimeter design.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md

Retained 25 mm as the aggressive innermost tracker envelope. It remains a host boundary, not a selected sensor radius; pipe/module clearances will be resolved in tracker design.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md

Recorded outer-solenoid bending, stray field and the need for a return yoke as a dedicated magnetic-system research question, outside the present envelope decision.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md

Detailed magnetic-system design is explicitly deferred to the next research task. This revision changes only its space reservation and the neighbouring envelopes.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md

Replaced the 200 mm shell with a 400 mm planning reservation, r=1.24–1.64 m and |z|≤3.55 m. The budget is 100 mm inner cryostat/interfaces + 150 mm cold assembly + 100 mm outer interfaces + 50 mm margin; 250 mm end allowances surround a cold assembly to |z|=3.30 m. Built NbTi benchmarks and explicit current/force scaling justify the scale. ECal/HCal move outward and downstream, and the muon barrel starts at 4.35 m, retaining nominal calorimeter depths and gaps. The regenerated allocation has no rectangle overlaps. This is a conservative planning allowance for 3 T centrally, not a certified safe magnet design; detailed magnetic research remains next.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md
Space budget: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-solenoid-space-budget.md

Recorded ACTS installation as the next software-stack step for straight-line and full-field tracking. PROP-V01 retains the shared-field and convergence requirements. No installation or propagation is claimed in this envelope revision.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md

The outermost tracker layer is now the potential timing-layer baseline to investigate. Sensor/readout timing capability, forward coverage and service space will be resolved in tracker design; separate timing assemblies remain alternatives rather than the preferred baseline.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md

Recorded dedicated muon-setup research as the next task, including magnet alternatives and measurement requirements. No further muon design is required in this envelope round beyond its space allocation.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md
The baseline can be approved.

## Global envelope baseline — E1-R2, ready for further human review

Review round 2's remaining request was a justified space allowance for a **3 T central solenoid**. E1-R2 reserves **r=1.24–1.64 m, |z|≤3.55 m** and moves adjacent calorimeters outward/downstream. The explicit budget includes 150 mm cold assembly, 200 mm cryostat/interface space and 50 mm integration margin, with 250 mm end allowances. This is a conservative planning allocation, not engineering certification.

[Main proposal](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md) · [Solenoid space budget](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-solenoid-space-budget.md) · [Review 2 disposition](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-2.md) · [Review 1](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-review-1.md) · [Study catalogue](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/validation/DES-003-study-catalogue.md)

### Working baseline

- 14 TeV HL-LHC; tracker |η|<4, calorimeter |η|<5, muons |η|<3 with 3.5 stretch.
- Detached forward calorimeter included; technology selection follows later.
- Retain **25 mm aggressive tracker host radius**, distinct from active sensor radius.
- Investigate the **outermost tracker layer as the potential timing layer**.
- Detailed magnetic-system and muon setup research come next. ACTS installation is planned for straight-line and full-field propagation.

### Proposed envelope allocations

Metres; reflect positive z to negative z. Maximum radii enclose any future polygon corners. The forward instrumented reservation excludes still-unassigned external support/readout/shielding volumes.

| Allocation | r min–max | absolute z min–max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tracker assembly | 0.025–1.14 | 0–3.15 |
| Tracker interface reserve | 1.14–1.24 | 0–3.15 |
| Coil / cryostat reserve | 1.24–1.64 | 0–3.55 |
| ECal barrel | 1.7–2.06 | 0–3.5 |
| ECal endcaps | 0.18–2.06 | 3.65–4.01 |
| HCal barrel | 2.16–4.2 | 0–4.01 |
| HCal endcaps | 0.2–4.2 | 4.16–6.2 |
| Muon barrel allocation | 4.35–6.762 | 0–7.2 |
| Muon endcap allocation | 0.4–7 | 7.2–10.27 |
| Forward calorimeter reserve | 0.12–1.5 | 11.2–13.2 |

![E1-R2 r–z drawing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/figures/DES-003-envelope-rz.png)

The central radial/axial shifts retain nominal calorimeter thicknesses and shared gaps, reducing the muon barrel host by another 0.20 m. Conditional 16-sided face-normal depths decrease slightly; the main proposal reports that consequence. Detailed magnet design may later amend the reservation; no uniform 3 T field map is claimed.

### Checks and decision scope

- 11 analytic envelope tests and 15 logging/documentation tests passed; 24 session records validated.
- Regenerated drawing/report: 10 allocations, 21 sampled rays, no positive-area rectangle overlaps. Input/script hashes verified and figure inspected.
- No detector transport, field solution, ACTS installation or performance acceptance claimed.

DES-003 and ADR-006 remain **DRAFT**. The requested human decision is the global envelope baseline and its explicit allowances. Subsequent subsystem/field/material work and resulting envelope amendments retain the normal design workflow. Only an identified human may sign off an exact revision. Production geometry and the TDR submodule are unchanged.

COMMENTED

Added operational ATLAS electron/photon and CMS hadron-calorimeter calibration papers alongside the TDR precedents. CAL-V01/02 now require material scenarios and species/energy/angle leakage studies. Historical depth bands remain screening ranges, not automatic containment requirements; 14 TeV collisions do not imply 14 TeV single-particle tests.

COMMENTED

Kept coil ordering and return topology coupled to the muon-system study. E1-R1 still draws an inner-solenoid hypothesis; outer-solenoid, instrumented-return and air-core-toroid alternatives remain. This iteration does not force a dedicated muon magnet decision.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Added ATLAS barrel/endcap-gap services (2008 detector paper §5.5, PDF166), CMS ECal end patch panels (§4.2, PDF119), and HGCAL outer-surface/rear-annular exits shared with timing/muons (TDR §4.5, PDF64–65). Proposed route topology: barrel bundles toward end patch regions, endcap bundles toward outer/rear handoffs, with named owners and phi sectors. Capacities and minimal path depth remain ENV-V03/CAL-V02 work.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md
COMMENTED

The proposal now calls for minimal but sufficient supports with explicit footprints and material ownership. Forward support, readout and shielding may extend beyond the instrumented box; its bounds are not advertised as a complete installed enclosure.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Made polygon shape an optional later component choice. Circular maximum-enclosure bounds remain the planning convention. The 16-sided depth calculation is explicitly conditional, retained only to compare with ODD.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-calorimeter-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Replaced the identification-first preference with a standalone-compatible, potentially toroidal baseline investigation. All three architectures remain in the comparison. Reserving the muon host is not proof that toroid coils, supports and stations fit; dedicated magnet design remains deferred.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Standalone-compatible muon measurement is now the baseline investigation rather than a mandatory finalized requirement. The catalogue separates tracker-combined, vertex-constrained muon-only and unconstrained standalone results, so an outer-coil combined fit cannot silently stand in for independent momentum measurement.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Recorded 14 TeV HL-LHC as the study scenario. CAL-V03/MU-V05 require leakage and punch-through evidence before recommending extra absorber steel. None is added. The detached forward calorimeter is downstream of current muon stations, so smaller upstream endcap apertures are proposed to study filtering at eta 3–3.5; their adequate depth remains unproven.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Recorded tracker |eta|<4, calorimeter |eta|<5 with extension conditional, and muons |eta|<3 with 3.5 stretch. E1-R1 proposes ECal/HCal inner endcap radii 0.18/0.20 m, muon parent 0.40 m and detached forward calorimetry. These are new draft allocations, not achieved acceptance; actual station edges need a later layout.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Added docs/validation/DES-003-study-catalogue.md, including MU-V01–08: stations, independent measurements, vector-field bending, material/transport, punch-through, sensitive hits, reconstruction and systematic variations. Every item lists owners, dependencies, outputs and execution state.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Added later operational calibration evidence. It supports the built scale and coverage but does not certify nODD containment: response corrections, material and leakage still matter. The cross-check also found a real documentation discrepancy: the 2008 CMS paper gives HF outer steel/sensitive radius 1.30 m, while the 2020 calibration paper §2 gives calorimeter radius 1.57 m. Its cause is unresolved and is not silently treated as an upgrade; nODD 1.50 m is an independent design proposal.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Built NbTi examples support studying 2–4 T, but not claiming that 3 T fits a complete 200 mm coil/cryostat. For a finite current sheet R=1.34 m, L=6.70 m, 3 T centrally needs about 17.23 MA-turn; magnetic-pressure scale is 3.58 MPa and a uniform-bore energy proxy is 115.9 MJ. The same toy model gives only 1.82 T on axis at z=3.15 m. Winding, reinforcement, thermal/quench systems and return flux need a physical decomposition; these calculations are not a magnet feasibility certificate.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Added mandatory PROP-V01 after a field and material/active-surface model exist. It requires full charged-particle propagation, sensitive crossings, numerical convergence and the same field identity in transport and reconstruction. Straight rays remain only the present allocation screen.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/validation/DES-003-study-catalogue.md
COMMENTED

Retained E1 central dimensions as the negotiation baseline. E1-R1 changes endcap apertures and adds forward calorimetry in response to the coverage review. The initial proposal is preserved at commit 7bb7ff0; new dimensions remain draft choices.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md
COMMENTED

A separate outer barrel timing assembly plus forward disks is the strongest comparison, rather than assuming an ordinary outer strip layer gives precision timing. CMS MTD provides a 40 mm barrel precedent using LYSO/SiPM; ATLAS HGTD provides forward LGAD coverage 2.4–4 with a 125 mm vessel/moderator allocation. Full nODD timing to eta 4 would be a new combined ambition. Coverage needs active-area/vertex/curved-track association, ageing, inefficiency and timing-response studies (TIME-V01); shared service space is not yet partitioned.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Retained the overall ODD-like starting scale and documented E1-R1 as a review-driven iteration. This agreement to start is recorded as direction for the investigation, not technical sign-off of numerical dimensions.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/DES-003-global-envelopes.md
COMMENTED

Dedicated muon-magnet selection/design remains with the later muon-system work. The current plan preserves standalone-compatible space and interface questions while comparing toroidal, solenoidal/combined and instrumented-return options.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md
COMMENTED

There is no justified universal minimum from collision energy alone. CMS Phase-2 TDR starts active pixels near 29 mm; operating ATLAS IBL provides a 33 mm precedent. We propose screening active radii around 30–35 mm later. The existing 25 mm host boundary is not a sensor radius: the inherited 24.4 mm pipe leaves only 0.6 mm before support, motion and installation allowance. Beam optics/aperture, pipe stability, lifetime/rate and module/support assumptions must set the limit.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-physics-review-1.md
COMMENTED

An outer solenoid can provide useful bending between tracker and muon segments, potentially replacing a separate magnet for a combined measurement. It does not automatically give tracker-independent momentum, particularly for displaced muons. Iron is not fundamentally required: flux can return through air or return coils, but the field/stray-field, energy and support problem changes. Compare signed bending integrals between measured surfaces, field maps, alignment and scattering; CMS operational yoke studies are now catalogued as evidence.

Details: https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/design/global-envelopes/docs/design/inputs/DES-003-muon-review-1.md
COMMENTED

Replaced the open coverage question with the explicit 4/5/3 targets and 3.5 muon stretch. The follow-up now asks whether proposed apertures, transition depth, finite vertices and upstream filtering can deliver those objectives.

## Proposed approach

I recommend **six candidate configurations**, compared in stages, with a review before detailed optimization. The team’s planning inputs are consolidated in [MAGNET_RESEARCH_PLAN.md]([redacted]

The central question is:

> Which configuration provides useful tracking and muon measurements across our coverage, with credible magnet, material and space requirements?

### 1. Candidate configurations

| ID | Configuration | Main question |
|---|---|---|
| MAG-01 | Inner solenoid, no dedicated return yoke | How much can tracker-assisted muon measurement achieve? |
| MAG-02 | Inner solenoid with instrumented iron return | Does additional bending justify the material and space? |
| MAG-03 | Solenoid outside central calorimeters, no dedicated yoke | Can tracker-to-muon bending replace a separate muon magnet? |
| MAG-04 | Outer solenoid with instrumented iron return | How suitable is a CMS-like arrangement at nODD scale? |
| MAG-05 | Inner solenoid plus air-core barrel/endcap toroids | Can we support independent muon momentum measurement within credible envelopes? |
| MAG-06 | Solenoid with active return/shielding coils | Can return coils reduce the need for a massive yoke? |

MAG-06 would receive a quick feasibility assessment first. End-compensation coils and other hybrids remain brainstorming options.

Two definitions matter:

- **“No dedicated yoke” does not mean no magnetic steel:** calorimeter absorbers and supports must be considered.
- **“Outside calorimeters” must specify barrel and endcaps.** The detached forward calorimeter remains a separate interface.

### 2. Team responsibilities

| Role | Main responsibility |
|---|---|
| **Project Coordinator** | Define candidates, common assumptions, comparison criteria and decision points. |
| **System Architect** | Coordinate physical interfaces and document required changes to the reviewed envelopes. |
| **Calorimeter engineer** | Compare upstream coil material against a larger external magnet; assess conversions, dead material, leakage, field exposure and services. |
| **Muon engineer** | Assess preferred configurations separately for independent momentum measurement and tracker-combined measurement; examine station spacing and forward gaps. |
| **Tracker engineer** | Assess useful bending to **|η| < 4**, finite-solenoid end effects, low-momentum trajectories and timing-layer crossings. |
| **Physics and Performance office** | Define representative particles and observables; challenge assumptions and distinguish performance gains from changes in size or material. |
| **Software coordinator** | Build verified field models, ACTS propagation, numerical checks and field displays. |
| **Publication office** | Maintain candidate summaries, source provenance, comparison figures, decisions and TDR-ready documentation. |

### 3. Work sequence

#### A. Define a fair comparison

Prepare a short specification for each candidate: coils, currents, return path, material assumptions, envelope demands and unresolved questions.

Initially:

- Normalize to **3 T at the interaction point**.
- Use the same tracker allocation and simple diagnostic measurement surfaces.
- Compare fixed layouts before allowing candidate-specific optimization.
- Then assess whether each configuration has credible current, stored-energy, force, material and space demands.

Equal central field alone does not mean equal tracking performance.

**First review:** agree the candidate set and comparison criteria.

#### B. Establish trustworthy field calculations

Use increasing modelling detail:

1. Analytic finite-solenoid checks and **Biot–Savart integration** for current-only models.
2. Three-dimensional coil models for discrete toroids and asymmetric arrangements.
3. Magnetostatic calculations with material response and saturation for iron-containing configurations.

A vacuum field multiplied by a permeability factor would not adequately model a return yoke.

Produce a consistent field-map format with units, coordinates, signs, interpolation, validity boundaries and provenance.

#### C. Verify propagation, then compare configurations

Start with:

- Zero-field straight lines.
- Uniform-field helices.
- Analytic solenoid checks.
- Charge/field reversal.
- Field-map interpolation and propagation-step convergence.

Then run ACTS trajectories through each candidate, sampling both charges, momentum ranges, central/forward directions, transition regions and toroid azimuthal sectors.

**Installation correction:** public PyPI’s `acts` is the Android Comms Test Suite. We should confirm an intended custom distribution or use the official tracking-ACTS build and Python bindings. ACTS documents straight-line and fourth-order Runge–Kutta steppers. [PyPI metadata]([external URL redacted; see source journal]), [ACTS bindings]([external URL redacted; see source journal]), [propagation documentation]([external URL redacted; see source journal]).

#### D. Assess detector consequences

Compare:

- Useful bending **between measurement surfaces**, including reversals and cancellations.
- Forward tracking leverage and lost crossings.
- Tracker-only, combined and genuinely independent muon measurements.
- Material before ECal and between muon stations.
- Scattering, energy loss, stray fields and envelope changes.

Add simplified measurement uncertainties and material scenarios after the field-only comparison. Shower containment and punch-through remain separate transport studies.

**Second review:** shortlist configurations and identify the evidence needed to distinguish them.

### 4. Deliverables

The research should produce:

- Six candidate summaries and a source/assumption register.
- Reproducible field and propagation tools.
- Field maps, trajectory overlays and publication-quality figures.
- A subsystem comparison matrix.
- Explicit envelope-amendment requests.
- A recommendation with uncertainties and remaining questions.

**My recommended first increment:** candidate definitions, verified ACTS setup, and the vacuum-solenoid benchmark. That establishes the foundation before investing in detailed yoke and toroid models.

Only planning documents, source records and the session journal were prepared; no installation or research execution has started. Local `main` still needs synchronization with merged PR #4 before execution.

## Coordinator: define the comparison contract

Keep **E1-R2 as the unchanged reference allocation**. Study magnetic configurations separately; document every required change to calorimeter, muon, support or service envelopes as an explicit amendment. No candidate should gain an advantage through undeclared extra space or material.

Use a manageable candidate set:

| ID | Magnetic configuration |
| --- | --- |
| N1 | Inner solenoid; no dedicated return yoke |
| N2 | Solenoid outside the central calorimeters; no dedicated return yoke |
| N3 | Inner or outer solenoid with an instrumented iron return; distinguish these variants |
| N4 | Inner solenoid plus an air-core toroidal muon system |
| N5 | Solenoid with active return coils; exploratory alternative |

“No dedicated yoke” does **not** mean an iron-free detector: ferromagnetic HCal absorbers and other steel affect flux, saturation and forces. Include their provisional distributions consistently.

### Compare in two stages

1. **Fixed central field:** normalize candidates to 3 T at the interaction point. Compare spatial field, bending between measured surfaces, upstream material, calorimeter exposure, stray field and required envelope changes. A common central field does not imply equal magnetic performance.
2. **Comparable resources:** assess conductor/current margins, stored energy, structural and cryostat space, service requirements and material. Determine whether each normalized configuration is credible within its allocation. Do not select a winner solely from the first comparison.

## Calorimeter role: assess material and integration consequences

An inner solenoid preserves the current ordering but puts coil, cryostat and associated services before ECal. Its consequences include upstream showers, conversion, energy loss and transition nonuniformity.

An outer solenoid removes that particular pre-ECal material but requires a larger bore and couples magnet supports to calorimeter installation and services. Coil material downstream can also affect leakage measurements and the path to muon stations.

For every candidate, distinguish instrumented calorimeter depth from coil, support and return material. Keep the detached forward calorimeter baseline visible; “outside calorimeters” must specify **outside central calorimeters**, since the forward system is longitudinally separate.

## Muon role: preference depends on the measurement requirement

For **independent standalone momentum**, N4 is the baseline investigation: bending among muon stations can support an independent measurement without a massive iron return. Fit within E1-R2, forward coverage and coil/support dead sectors remain unproven.

For **tracker-combined momentum and identification**, N2 could be sufficient and simpler. Demonstrate bending between measured surfaces; distinguish tracker-constrained, vertex-constrained and unconstrained standalone fits.

N3 offers return-field bending but introduces scattering, saturation and material complexity. N5 deserves an initial feasibility screen before detailed work.

### Physics and tracker contribution to the magnetic research plan

**Objective:** compare magnetic architectures against the agreed 14 TeV scope—tracking to |η|≈4, calorimetry to ≈5, muons to ≈3 with 3.5 as a stretch objective—without selecting detailed tracker layers.

**Candidate matrix.** Evaluate seven families: inner solenoid with calorimeter steel as its return path; inner solenoid with additional return yoke; outer solenoid with calorimeter steel as return; outer solenoid with dedicated return yoke; inner solenoid plus air-core toroid; inner solenoid plus iron-dominated toroidal return; and solenoid with active return coils. The architect must specify a physically consistent return path for each; a family label alone is insufficient.

**Common diagnostic detector.** Agree a small set of barrel cylinders and forward disks spanning the current tracker allocation, plus common muon measurement stations. Label them diagnostic surfaces, not proposed layers. Use identical measurement uncertainties and fitting conventions initially. Evaluate architecture-specific station adjustments separately so improved field and increased detector size are distinguishable.

**Field observables.** Map the vector field throughout tracking and muon regions. Along representative trajectories, report transverse bending, bending direction and its variation, field reversals, and measurement leverage. Central field and an unsigned integral of field magnitude are insufficient: forward tracks can travel nearly parallel to a solenoidal field, and opposing bends can cancel.

**Reconstruction observables.** Compare curvature information, charge discrimination and momentum uncertainty versus momentum and direction. Keep three results separate:

- Tracker-only measurement.
- Muon standalone measurement without tracker or interaction-point constraint.
- Combined tracker–muon measurement, with vertex-constrained fits shown separately.

Add crossings, acceptance losses and material before calorimeters.

**Staged comparison.** Begin with straight trajectories and field diagnostics. Then propagate charged particles and fit the common surfaces without scattering. Finally introduce stated material and scattering models. Use a small diagnostic grid covering central, transition, forward and coverage-edge directions; sample both charges, distinct bending regimes and relevant azimuths for toroids. Refine only where gradients, cancellations or acceptance transitions demand it. Grid points and uncertainties are study settings, not performance requirements.

**Fairness controls.** Publish fixed-layout comparisons before optimized-layout comparisons, with explicit field-only, material-only and combined effects.

**Major pitfalls:** assuming uniform forward field; concealing a vertex constraint in “standalone” performance; confusing material absorption with useful muon bending; comparing differently optimized reconstruction; and declaring superiority before an agreed cost, size and material tradeoff exists.

## Proposed software work package

**First correct the installation assumption:** public PyPI’s `acts` package is the unrelated **Android Comms Test Suite**. We should not execute `pip install acts`. Tracking ACTS documents a CMake build with Python bindings; choose and pin that build or a compatible prepared environment. [PyPI package]([external URL redacted; see source journal]), [ACTS installation]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

### 1. Establish the supported propagation environment

After discussion, check the selected ACTS revision against local macOS architecture, compiler, Python ABI and dependencies. The existing Python 3.14 environment is not automatically compatible.

ACTS provides `StraightLineStepper` and `EigenStepper`; the latter uses fourth-order Runge–Kutta integration. Its Python examples demonstrate `acts.EigenStepper(field)`, `acts.Propagator(...)` and the examples propagation wrapper. Verify the precise straight-line binding and constructors in the pinned release before writing our adapter. Describe this as **ACTS field propagation using its RK4-family stepper**, not a new custom fixed-step RK4 implementation. [Propagation documentation]([external URL redacted; see source journal]), [Python example]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

### 2. Separate field calculation from particle propagation

Proposed hierarchy:

- Current-only finite solenoids: analytic/Biot–Savart models, explicitly neglecting magnetic material.
- Ferromagnetic return structures: nonlinear magnetostatic calculation using justified B–H curves, saturation, boundaries and mesh convergence. Multiplying the vacuum field by a permeability factor is inadequate.
- Discrete toroid coils: three-dimensional field calculation, retaining coil sectors and end effects.

ACTS supplies an analytical solenoid provider and interpolated field maps; these can support the first screening studies without inventing another field interface. [ACTS field providers]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

### 3. Define a common map contract

Use axisymmetric `Br(r,z), Bz(r,z)` maps only for justified rotational symmetry. Use full three-component 3D maps for discrete toroids and asymmetric return structures. Record coordinate conventions, units, reflection rules, domain, interpolation, current normalization and out-of-domain behavior.

### 4. Verify before comparing architectures

Plan zero-field straight-line and uniform-field helix benchmarks; finite-solenoid axis checks; charge/field reversal; field symmetry and divergence diagnostics away from singularities; mesh, interpolation and propagation-step convergence. Compare signed bending integrals and station displacement, not only central field magnitude.

Start with vacuum trajectories; introduce material and active surfaces explicitly afterward. This advances **FIELD-V01, PROP-V01 and MU-V03**, while preserving their distinction from momentum-resolution or shower-performance claims.
